summary.text: Amy Acton is a physician and public health researcher from Youngstown who served as Ohio Department of Health director under Republican Gov. Mike DeWine from 2019 to 2020, leading the state's early COVID-19 response. She is the Democratic nominee for governor, running with David Pepper. Her campaign centers on an affordability agenda that includes child tax credits, an online prescription-drug platform called Ohio Rx, and a conditional moratorium on data-center expansion.

paragraphs.text: Amy Acton was born in Youngstown, Ohio, and earned a bachelor's degree from Youngstown State University and a medical degree from Northeast Ohio Medical University in 1990.
She completed residencies in pediatrics and preventive medicine and earned a master's in public health from Ohio State University.
Acton taught public health at Ohio State University, where an Associated Press report describes her as an associate professor, and worked at the Columbus Foundation.
Gov. Mike DeWine appointed her Director of the Ohio Department of Health in February 2019; she left the post in June 2020.
She remained as the governor's chief health adviser until August 2020.
After leaving state government, Acton returned to the Columbus Foundation and later directed the city of Columbus's Project L.O.V.E., a childhood vaccination initiative.
She has not previously held elective office and launched her campaign for governor in January 2025.
